class_id: a drift check compares declared-to-live in one direction only, so an object hand-applied live and never declared is invisible to it
symptom: a schema-drift audit built to catch 'schema.ts says X, the live DB does not have X' only ever walks the declared side and asks whether each declared object exists live. An object that exists live but was never added to schema.ts (a hand-applied index or constraint) has no declared counterpart to walk from, so it is invisible to the check -- and a later `drizzle-kit generate` run against the undeclared-but-real live object can silently propose to drop it. Universal shape: any two-sided reconciliation (declared vs. live, expected vs. actual, config vs. deployed) that is coded from only one side's enumeration structurally cannot detect an extra object on the other side.
first_seen: 2026-09-16 (found by lane C while fixing the duplicate-IPO merge tool, #662/PR #664), fixed 2026-09-26 (#665, PR #1204). Staging's `ipos_symbol_key` UNIQUE constraint exists live (pg_indexes/pg_constraint) but was never declared in packages/shared/src/db/schema.ts, which carries only `index('idx_ipos_symbol')`. `npm run audit:schema-drift` compared columns and declared-to-live objects only, so index/constraint drift in the undeclared direction was invisible on both prod and staging.
fix_prs: #1204: adds `diffUndeclaredIndexes()`/`diffUndeclaredUniqueConstraints()`, pure functions over plain live-row data, plus async wiring `checkUndeclaredIndexes()`/`checkUndeclaredUniqueConstraints()`. Matches a declared `.unique()` to its live backing object by (table, column) identity rather than by name -- Postgres's own default naming (`_key` suffix) and drizzle's default naming (`_unique` suffix) both occur live on the same schema depending on how the original migration was hand-written; measured on staging, admin_settings/ipo_details/ipo_financials/ipo_slug_redirects all declare `.unique()` but carry `_key`-suffixed live constraints, so a name-only match would have false-positived on all four. Excludes PK-backing and unique-backing automatic indexes/constraints generically. One reviewed allow-list entry for a legacy constraint.
detection_check: checkUndeclaredIndexes()/checkUndeclaredUniqueConstraints() in assert-schema-drift.ts, run via `npm run audit:schema-drift`.
